title: Supabase
content:
## Overview

Supabase is an open-source Firebase alternative that provides a PostgreSQL database, authentication, instant APIs, edge functions, realtime subscriptions, and storage. Emergent supports Supabase as a backend integration, allowing your AI-built applications to leverage enterprise-grade data storage and user authentication.

This guide walks you through connecting your Emergent app to Supabase and using its core features.

## What you can do with Supabase

- **PostgreSQL database**: Store structured data with the full power of a relational database
- **Built-in authentication**: Email/password, OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, etc.), magic links
- **Realtime subscriptions**: Listen to database changes and update your UI instantly
- **Row-level security**: Define fine-grained access policies directly in the database
- **Storage**: Upload and serve user files with access control
- **Edge functions**: Run server-side logic close to your users

## Prerequisites

- A Supabase account ([sign up free](https://supabase.com))
- A Supabase project with your database and auth configured
- Your Supabase project URL and anon/public API key (found in Project Settings → API)

## Connecting Supabase to your Emergent app

<Steps>
<Step title="Add Supabase credentials to your app">
In your Emergent chat, tell the AI to add Supabase as a data source. You'll need:

- **Project URL**: `https://your-project.supabase.co`
- **Anon key**: Your public API key (safe to expose in client code)

Example prompt:
```
Add Supabase integration. My project URL is https://abc123.supabase.co 
and anon key is eyJhbGc... Use it for user authentication and to store 
tasks in a 'tasks' table.
```

The AI will install the Supabase client library and configure the connection.
</Step>

<Step title="Define your database schema">
Describe your data model in chat, and the AI will either:

- Generate SQL migrations to run in the Supabase SQL Editor, or
- Use the Supabase client to create tables programmatically

<Tip>
For production apps, use Supabase's migration system in the Dashboard → Database → Migrations. This keeps your schema under version control.
</Tip>

Example:
```
Create a 'profiles' table with columns: id (uuid), email (text), 
display_name (text), created_at (timestamp). Add a foreign key 
to auth.users(id).
```
</Step>

<Step title="Set up authentication">
Tell the AI which auth methods you want (email/password, OAuth, magic links). The AI will:

- Configure the Supabase auth client
- Create sign-up, sign-in, and sign-out flows
- Handle session persistence
- Protect routes that require authentication

Example:
```
Add email/password sign-up and sign-in. Show a login form on the 
home page. After login, redirect to /dashboard.
```
</Step>

<Step title="Implement data operations">
Describe CRUD operations in natural language. The AI translates them into Supabase queries.

Example prompts:
```
When a user creates a task, insert a row in the tasks table with 
title, description, user_id, and completed=false.
```

```
On the dashboard, fetch all tasks for the current user where 
completed=false, ordered by created_at desc.
```

The AI will use `supabase.from('table').select()`, `.insert()`, `.update()`, and `.delete()` methods.
</Step>

<Step title="Add row-level security (RLS)">
For secure multi-user apps, describe access rules and the AI will generate RLS policies or guide you to add them in the Supabase Dashboard.

Example:
```
Enable RLS on the tasks table. Users can only see and edit their own tasks.
```

<Warning title="Enable RLS for sensitive data">
Without row-level security, any client with the anon key can read or modify all rows. Always enable RLS policies for tables containing user data.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Test and iterate">
Use Emergent's preview to test authentication flows and data operations. If something doesn't work, describe the issue in chat and the AI will debug and fix it.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common patterns

### Realtime subscriptions

To listen for live database changes:

```
When a new task is inserted, append it to the task list in realtime 
without refreshing the page.
```

The AI will set up a Supabase subscription using `.on('INSERT', callback)`.

### File storage

To upload and serve images or documents:

```
Add a profile picture upload. Store images in a Supabase storage bucket 
called 'avatars' and display the user's avatar in the header.
```

The AI will configure storage buckets and handle file uploads with `supabase.storage.from('bucket').upload()`.

### Server-side logic with Edge Functions

For operations that shouldn't run in the browser (webhooks, scheduled jobs, sensitive business logic):

```
Create a Supabase Edge Function that sends a daily email summary 
of completed tasks.
```

<Note>
Emergent can generate the function code, but you'll deploy it manually via the Supabase CLI or Dashboard.
</Note>

## Environment variables

The AI stores Supabase credentials as environment variables:

- `SUPABASE_URL`
- `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (for admin operations, **never expose client-side**)

These are automatically injected at runtime. You don't need to configure them manually unless deploying outside Emergent.

## Comparison with other integrations

| Feature | Supabase | [MongoDB](/database-mongodb) |
|---------|----------|------------------------------|
| Data model | Relational (SQL) | Document (NoSQL) |
| Built-in auth | ✅ Yes | ❌ No (use separate service) |
| Realtime | ✅ Native subscriptions | Requires Change Streams setup |
| File storage | ✅ Built-in | Separate GridFS or S3 |
| Best for | Structured data, user auth | Flexible schemas, rapid iteration |

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Error: Invalid API key">
Check that you're using the **anon key** (not the service role key) for client-side code. Verify the key in Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Users can see each other's data">
Enable row-level security (RLS) policies on your tables. In the Supabase Dashboard, go to Authentication → Policies and create rules like:

```sql
CREATE POLICY "Users see own tasks" ON tasks
  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Authentication redirects not working">
Make sure your Supabase project has the correct Site URL and Redirect URLs configured in Authentication → URL Configuration. For Emergent preview URLs, you may need to add wildcard patterns.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Realtime subscriptions not triggering">
Confirm that Realtime is enabled for your table in Database → Replication. Also check that RLS policies allow the user to SELECT the rows they're subscribing to.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
